display.title: Episode 417: The Overturned Inkwell
display.summary_short: Why we cover our eyes for the Shema, a guest from Australia, a listener's phone quiz on 'Echad', and the story of a rabbi who proves to a king that the world has a Creator.
display.summary_long: Broadcast in late Shevat 5750. Mitzvah Time teaches something unique about the Shema: we close our eyes and cover them with the right hand so nothing distracts us, and we say each word slowly with the kavanah of Echad. After the Hakochainik march, a third-grade girl visiting from Sydney, Australia says the Shema in Studio 604 and describes what she learns and the Tzivos Hashem gift wallet with the Twelve Pesukim. A recorded phone call follows in which a boy from Monsey answers questions on the letters of Echad, and everyone gives tzedakah. The story explains why the Torah opens with Creation before any laws: a king asks a wise rabbi why we cannot say the world simply made itself. When the king knocks over his inkwell and leaves the room, the rabbi paints a beautiful landscape and tells the king the spilled ink made it. 'Impossible!' says the king, and the rabbi points to the world outside the window: so too, it must have a great Artist. The show closes with a call for sponsors to help expand the program, the sponsor, and candle time.
display.lesson: Nothing happens by itself: the beautiful world shows that Hashem alone created it and runs it.
